RICS Report Finds AI Adoption in Construction Still Low

By Adrian North Published On: September 16th, 2025 Categories: Top Stories
A new global report from the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) reveals that while artificial intelligence (AI) is seen as a game-changer for construction, actual adoption remains limited — with most firms yet to implement AI at scale.
The AI in Construction 2025 report is based on survey data from more than 2,200 construction professionals worldwide, including project managers, quantity surveyors, and senior decision-makers. The findings present a complex picture: growing enthusiasm for AI’s potential, but significant barriers to adoption on the ground.

Most Construction Firms Still Not Using AI

According to the report, 45% of organisations reported no current use of AI, while just 1% had managed to scale AI across their projects.

...

oject managers and quantity surveyors surveyed believe AI will help them deliver greater value, particularly in areas such as cost control, risk management, and project scheduling.

AI’s Biggest Impact Expected in Design Innovation

The report identifies design optioneering — the process of using algorithms to explore multiple design outcomes — as the most likely area to benefit from AI in the next five years. 40% of respondents expect AI to play a pivotal role in speeding up and enhancing project design.
Other high-potential areas include:
* Predictive scheduling
* Cost estimation and forecasting
* Contract and risk management
* BIM integration with AI-driven tools

Barriers to AI in Construction: Skills, Data, and Integration

The report identifies several critical barriers holding back adoption:
* Lack of skilled personnel – cited by 46% of respondents
* System integration issues – cited by 37%

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING APPLICATIONS IN CONSTRUCTION PROJECT MANAGEMENT: ENHANCING SCHEDULING, COST ESTIMATION, AND RISK MITIGATION

Authors

* Md.

...

Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Construction Project Management, Cost Overrun, Risk Mitigation, BIM Integration

Abstract

Chronic schedule slippage, cost overruns, and safety incidents remain persistent in construction projects, yet empirical, project-level evidence connecting artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) adoption to core delivery outcomes is limited. This study’s purpose is to quantify how AI/ML adoption relates to schedule adherence, cost estimation accuracy, and risk mitigation effectiveness. We apply a quantitative, cross-sectional, multi-case design using enterprise-scale construction cases sampled across multiple firms. The sample comprises 102 projects meeting strict inclusion criteria for verifiable baselines, actuals, and risk registers. Key variables include an AI/ML Adoption Index 0–100 capturing use-case breadth, run frequency, model sophistication, and integration depth; outcomes are Schedule Delay percent, Cost Overrun percent, Risk Detection Rate, and Residual Risk Impact on a 1–5 scale; a Complexity Index and Digital Maturity serve as moderator and control alongside budget, duration, sector, contract type, and region.

...

Headline findings indicate that each 10-point rise in adoption associates with approximately 1.2 percentage points lower schedule delay, 0.9 percentage points lower cost overrun, 0.04 higher detection rate, and 0.06 lower residual severity, with effects amplified on higher-complexity projects.
